player.name: Pell Wicklow
player.concept: a nosy gnome tinker-wizard with too many pockets and a habit of talking to animals

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Late afternoon settles over the crossroads. A weathered milestone stands beside the empty gibbet; blackthorn hedges crowd the drovers’ track, and crows pick at a dead ox in the ditch. Smoke tangles with the wind, though no hearth is in sight.

A mud-caked farmer jabs his pitchfork at the hedge, then shouts at the milestone. His red-rimmed eyes and unsteady laugh suggest he hasn’t slept. “You tell ’em, stone! Little green devils in the hedges—” He spots you and wheels around, leveling the pitchfork. “Stay back! I know what you are!”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I stop dead, raise both hands (one still holding a half-eaten pear) and waggle my fingers. "Easy, friend, easy! Pinkish, see? Not a speck of green on me, unless you count the moss stain on my left knee." I nod politely at the milestone. "What's the stone been telling you, then? I've always found milestones terrible conversationalists. All numbers, no gossip."

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Tam’s pitchfork dips. He grabs your sleeve with his free hand, then seems to realize he’s doing it and lets go.

“Right. Pinkish. Yes. You’ve got the look of a person who knows a stone can’t gossip.” His laugh comes out too loud. “Ox was theirs, though. Crude arrows in the poor beast, and little green devils slipping through the hedges after me since dawn. Told the tollhouse, I did. They said cider.”

He glances toward the blackthorn, then rubs the front of his smock as if checking something’s still there. “I only want to get home to Bet. Hollis Farm, down the track. You’ll believe me, won’t you?”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: "Hollis Farm!" I clap my hands, pear and all. "Hold on, not the Hollis with the weathervane shaped like a goose in a bonnet? I fixed that goose! Must be fifteen years back. Squeaked something awful in a westerly." I tap the side of my nose. "And Bet, is she your wife? Does she still make that plum tart with the burnt top?" I glance at his smock. "And you can stop patting your belly, friend. I'm not a pickpocket. Well. Not professionally."

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Tam gives you a startled look, then a shaky nod. “Goose bonnet? Aye! Still squeaks, but Bet says it keeps the sparrows off. And the tart—well, burnt top’s the best bit, ain’t it?”

For a moment, the terror eases from his face. When you glance at his smock, he only gives a nervous little laugh. “Not patting my belly. Making sure my heart’s still in there, that’s all. Goblins’ll do that to a man.”

He tells you again about the arrows, the ox, the green shapes darting between the hedges. He seems frightened and sincere. “Walk with me to the farm? Please. Just till I’m home with Bet.”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: "Course I'll walk you home, Tam. Only, one moment." I trot over to the ditch and crouch a polite distance from the crows, holding out my pear core like a calling card. "Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen of the ditch. Fine ox. My condolences to the ox. I don't suppose any of you saw who put the arrows in him? I'd pay in pear." While I wait for an answer I squint at the arrows sticking out of the carcass.

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
The crows shuffle closer, bold as old landlords. One croaks, then another answers from the ox’s back. At your offer, the largest snatches the pear core and flaps up to the milestone.

The arrows are crude, short shafts of dark wood, fletched with ragged black feathers. The wounds around them are old enough that the blood has gone tacky.

Behind you, Tam says, “You’ll come with me, then? Bet’ll put the kettle on.” His hand drifts to the same spot beneath his smock. The crows suddenly lift as one, wings beating hard. From somewhere inside the blackthorn comes a dry, rattling sound.
